inputs.share_count_basis: 1,596.0m ordinary shares, unchanged since listing; no options, RSUs or convertibles outstanding (basic = diluted, FY2025 AR EPS note and H1 FY2026 interim). Held flat; no SBC and no buybacks.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet (RMB'000 / 1000). Cash = cash & equivalents 3,285.0 + restricted bank deposits 40.3 + term deposits 2,342.9 (current 1,445.2 + non-current 897.7; ~306m pledged against bills payable/borrowings, which are themselves liabilities in the debt/WC). Debt = bank borrowings 3,485.1 + lease liabilities 103.8 (27.6 current + 76.2 non-current). Wealth-management products (FVTPL 10,186.3) are NOT in this cash figure; they enter via equity_bridge at fair value less a 10% haircut.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 finance income was RMB190.6m and FVTPL gains RMB263.9m, but neither is inside reported FCF: HKFRS cash flow classifies interest received (RMB108.4m) in INVESTING and FVTPL gains are reversed out of cash generated from operations. Reported FCF (OCF 3,479.8 - PP&E capex 1,284.1) is therefore already ex-treasury income, so no further deduction (deducting again would double-strip). In the forward build, EBITDA margins exclude the FVTPL gains (inside 'other gains - net' in operating profit) because the WMP asset is in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme disclosed in FY2017-FY2025 annual reports or H1 FY2026 interim; EquityAwardTaxes 0 and ShareRepurchases 0 in kpis. Genuine SBC-zero filer (not missing data).
inputs.fx_note: Model in CNY millions; per-share values converted CNY->HKD at 1.1724 HKD per CNY (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-16T21:47Z). Cross-rate check: USDHKD 7.8479 / USDCNY 6.6768 = 1.1754 (0.25% tie), confirming direction (HKD per CNY > 1). No dual listing to parity-check against. RMB has appreciated materially in 2026 (management cites it as an H1 margin headwind); refresh_price.py does not refresh this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z regular close (HKEX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta 1.1 x 7.0% China ERP = ~9.5% cost of equity; the group is net cash (borrowings are working-capital lines at ~2-3%), so WACC ~= cost of equity = 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, China-macro and overseas-capex risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked as a premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities RMB103.8m included in total_debt; lease principal (~RMB30m/yr) not deducted from flows; lease_cost_pct_path 0. Immaterial either way (<0.2% of revenue). ROU assets are mainly prepaid land use rights.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI tiny (RMB15.3m equity, RMB1.9m FY2025 profit). Flows are consolidated; NCI stock deducted once in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (CNY flows vs HKD quote, SBC-zero, matching-asset rule for treasury). ROUTING: Haitian is an operating manufacturer of injection moulding machines (95% machines, 5% parts/service) -- not a bank, REIT, LIC or holdco -- so routing-table row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). TREASURY JUDGMENT: the RMB10.2bn of bank/trust/fund wealth-management products and RMB2.3bn of term deposits are surplus cash parked for yield (management itself counts WMPs in its 'net cash' figure; diversified across 30+ institutions, floating 1.3-7.3%). They are treated as non-operating: term deposits in cash at par, WMPs in equity_bridge at fair value less a 10% haircut for trust/fund-product credit and liquidity risk and the PRC repatriation friction on cash held onshore. Their income (finance income + FVTPL gains, ~RMB450m in FY2025) is excluded from the forward EBITDA margin, so it is counted once. EBITDA BASIS: metrics EBITDA = operating profit + D&A and includes FVTPL gains (FY2025 263.9m, H1 FY2026 141.3m) and the H1 FY2026 one-off RMB97.1m gain on disposing Ningbo Haitian Guohua. Ex those, EBITDA margin was 23.2% FY2025, 23.5% FY2024, 21.2% H1 FY2026. It still includes recurring R&D government grants (RMB427.9m, 2.4% of revenue FY2025) -- kept in base/bull, faded in bear. Buybacks: none ever; flat count is the actual history, not a convention needing funding. FY0 is FY2025; the H1 FY2026 balance sheet is used for the bridge, so FY2026 flows are discounted a full year (slightly conservative).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: eps_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025). Equity CAGR overridden: book value is inflated by ~RMB10bn of retained treasury assets that earn 2-3%, not by operating reinvestment.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.3% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 6.6% (41% higher). 3-year CAGRs (FY2022-25) start from the FY2022 cyclical trough (revenue -23%) and overstate trend growth; the FCF 3yr CAGR of 97.5% is off a trough FCF of RMB285m and is meaningless.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF for every year (SBC zero, interest income already outside OCF), so owner-FCF and reported CAGRs coincide. FCF is lumpy because of working-capital swings (FY2024 revenue +RMB3.1bn absorbed ~RMB1.2bn of WC; FY2025 released it) and an overseas capex cycle (capex 7-12% of revenue FY2022-25 vs ~4-5% pre-2020). FY2020-25 average FCF ~RMB1.48bn; FY2025's 2.2bn includes a WC release. Through-cycle revenue growth FY2017-25 is 7.1%/yr.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +1%: H1 +0.9% with overseas -19.3% and no evidence of H2 acceleration. FY2027-28 recovery to ~6% (overseas plants in Mexico/Vietnam/Serbia/India ramp, restocking), decaying to 3% -- below the 7.1% FY2017-25 through-cycle rate because China domestic PIMM share (>80% local) is near saturation.
base.margin_rationale: Ex-FVTPL EBITDA margin 21.2% in H1 FY2026 (GM 31.1% on RMB strength and lower overseas mix) vs 23.2-23.5% FY2024-25. Recovers to 23.0% as overseas mix returns; no expansion beyond the FY2024-25 level.
base.capex_rationale: Capex has averaged 7.5% of revenue FY2017-25 (2.5x D&A of ~3%) as the overseas and domestic footprint kept expanding; H1 FY2026 4.5%. Path 5.5-6.0% near term gliding to 5.0% vs 3.6% D&A at terminal -- deliberately above the D&A-plus-growth minimum because this company has never run capex near D&A.
base.tax_rationale: Effective tax 17.5% (HNTE 15% at main PRC subsidiaries); cash tax paid / EBIT ~17% FY2025. 18% adds a little PRC dividend-withholding leakage on upstreaming to the Cayman parent.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables 5.8bn + inventory 4.3bn exceed payables 5.4bn + contract liabilities 1.2bn + accruals 1.9bn; growth consumes cash. -15% of incremental revenue, between FY2024 (-40%) and the long-run net-WC/revenue ratio (~9%).
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 12x binds (Gordon at 9.5%/2.5% = 14.6x) -- cyclical capital-goods maker.

scenario_narratives.base: Overseas Chinese-enterprise capex resumes after the H1 FY2026 energy-price pause and Haitian's localized plants (Mexico, Vietnam, Serbia, India, Japan) take share from European/Japanese makers abroad, while China domestic demand grows with NEV/3C reinvestment but daily-goods and appliance moulders stay soft. Revenue recovers to mid-single-digit growth from FY2027 and ex-treasury EBITDA margin returns to the 23% of FY2024-25 as overseas mix rebuilds; RMB strength is a lasting but not worsening headwind. R&D government grants (~2.4% of revenue) continue.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'Five-Five' internationalisation compounds: reshoring and supply-chain diversification by Chinese and global manufacturers drives overseas sales back to the FY2025 +26% trajectory, Zhafir electric and Jupiter large-tonnage machines win in the premium segment against Engel/Arburg/Fanuc, and parts & service grows its share. Revenue grows 7-9% for three years and margin expands to 24.5% on mix and scale procurement.
scenario_narratives.bear: A FY2022-style capex downturn (revenue then fell 23%): tariffs and sanctions on Chinese capital equipment cap the overseas engine, China domestic moulding demand stays weak, and low-end domestic rivals (Yizumi, Borche, Tederic) compete on price. Revenue falls 2% in FY2026 and 8% in FY2027 before a slow recovery; margin compresses to 18.5-20% as RMB strength persists and local R&D subsidies fade; cash tax creeps up. Balance sheet is not at risk -- the bear is an earnings trough, not solvency.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: this is a high-cyclicality capital-goods maker whose overseas driver just reversed (-19.3% in H1 FY2026) with tariff and geopolitical exposure. Base 50% as the central recovery path. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs overseas recovery, premium-segment share gains and margin expansion to coincide. No solvency risk (large net treasury position) caps the bear at an earnings trough.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Haitian is valued as a cyclical operating manufacturer on owner FCF in CNY, with its large treasury (term deposits and wealth-management products, ~RMB12.5bn gross, ~RMB8/share net of borrowings after a 10% WMP haircut) valued separately in the bridge and its income removed from the flows. At the current price, the market capitalises the operating business at a low single-digit EV/EBITDA, i.e. it either discounts the treasury heavily (China-cash discount) or prices a deep cyclical downturn. SBC is genuinely zero, so house and street bases coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Treasury haircut: if the WMP/term-deposit pile is worth materially less to minority holders (trapped onshore, credit events in trust products, or never distributed), roughly half of per-share value is at stake.
Cyclicality: a FY2022-style -23% revenue year would cut owner FCF by half for one to two years.
Overseas growth reversal from tariffs, sanctions, or energy costs (H1 FY2026 overseas -19.3%).
RMB appreciation compressing export margins (~34-43% of sales are foreign-currency); also moves the CNY->HKD conversion of value.
Government R&D grants (~2.4% of revenue) are discretionary local subsidies.
Related-party transactions with the founding Zhang family group (e.g. the RMB336m Guohua disposal to a connected party).
